title: Embedding distance mode adapter and runtime compatibility shim
creator: Avery Chen
description: Problem: Customers depend on historical embedding scoring behavior (some clients relied on raw dot products, others on normalized cosine). Recent internal changes to vector normalization in the embedding pipeline and a default normalization flag introduced small but important ranking differences that broke a handful of production rerankers. This ticket introduces a runtime adapter/shim that provides per-tenant compatibility modes for distance metric and normalization handling, minimizing regressions while enabling a path to a consistent, documented default.
acceptance_criteria: Add a per-request and per-tenant query parameter/setting 'metric_mode' supporting 'dot', 'cosine', and 'euclidean' that controls scoring behavior
Default production behavior remains unchanged for existing tenants (no silent change to ranking outcomes)
New API docs describe metric semantics and normalization flags; SDKs expose the option consistently
Benchmarks for latency and throughput for each mode exist and show <5% p95 latency regression for cosine compared to dot when caching/fast-paths are enabled
Unit and integration tests cover: raw dot, normalized cosine (pre-normalize vectors server-side), mixed inputs (already-normalized vectors from client), and migration path scenarios
Rollout plan exists to gradually enable metric_mode opt-in for customers and to default new customers to documented behaviour
Migration helper tool to scan historical embeddings (per-customer) and recommend a metric_mode or re-normalization batch is available
implementation_plan: Design: define runtime scoring interface that accepts (vector_a, vector_b, metadata) and a metric_mode enum
Data model: extend embedding metadata store to optionally keep precomputed norm (float16) and a flag 'client_normalized'

Runtime: implement three fast paths: (1) dot-fast (no extra work), (2) cosine-fast (use stored norm if available, else compute norm with SIMD/AVX path and cache), (3) euclidean (compute squared L2 efficiently)
API: add 'metric_mode' and 'normalize_on_server' query params to rerank endpoint; SDKs to surface defaults and warnings
Compat shim: per-tenant persisted setting default_metric_mode; if unset treat tenant as legacy-preserve and keep current behavior
Storage migration: backfill precomputed norms for high-volume tenants using background batch workers with rate limiting
Bench: create stress harness to measure tokenization/embedding retrieval + scoring latency under typical reranker QPS with beam size up to 64
PRs: split into small PRs: schema, runtime fast paths, API surface, SDK changes, migration tooling
risks: Incorrect assumptions about which tenants expect normalized vs raw dot semantics could cause ranking regressions if defaults are changed prematurely
Precomputing and storing norms increases storage and write amplification; need to quantify cost and implement float16 compression
Computing norms on the hot path without caching may increase p95 latency for cosine by >10% unless optimized kernels are used
Client-provided normalized vectors could be double-normalized if server-side normalization is naively applied; must honor 'client_normalized' flag
benchmarks: Local perf run (nvme instance): dot-fast p50=2.1ms p95=6.8ms throughput=1200r/s
Cosine with precomputed norms p50=2.3ms p95=7.2ms throughput=1150r/s
Cosine without precompute (compute norm on-request) p50=3.5ms p95=12.1ms throughput=800r/s
Euclidean scoring added ~0.4ms median due to extra ops when vector dim=1536
Memory overhead: storing float16 norm per vector = 2 bytes per vector; 1M vectors ~=2MB additional metadata (negligible)
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Merge schema + runtime shim behind feature flag in canary cluster (no default changes)
Phase 1: Enable per-tenant setting UI in Console for 10 pilot customers; run A/B evaluation against control for ranking parity
Phase 2: Background backfill precomputed norms for pilot tenants; monitor latency/cost metrics for 7 days
Phase 3: Expose metric_mode in public API and SDKs with explicit opt-in; provide migration guide and CLI tool
Phase 4: After 90% confidence in parity, update new customers to documented default (explicit in sign-up); do not silently change existing tenants
Phase 5: If product decides, offer an automated migration option that re-normalizes stored embeddings and flips tenant to cosine by consent
qa_notes: Test cases must include mixed-origin embeddings: server-generated, client-supplied normalized, and legacy stored vectors
Fuzz test scoring for numerical stability across dims [256,512,1024,1536,3072], different quantization formats (int8, q4) and for edge cases: zero vectors, NaNs
Integration test that validates rerank order is identical for legacy tenants after enabling shim in canary
Load test: 1k r/s sustained for 30 minutes with 95th percentile latency tracking for all three metric modes
